full_judgment:
5. In answer to the Rule, the respondents entered appearance and filed affidavits-in-opposition affirmed by a Section Officer of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of Bangladesh. In the said affidavits dated 15.1.75 and 20.2.75 it has been stated that the detenue has been detained lawfully in view of his past activities and also to prevent him from doing any prejudicial act. It has further been stated that he is not a national of Bangladesh and he along with his father other and members of his family migrated to India from Dacca in 1950 and settled in Calcutta at Kumartoli and installed a new temple there in the name of Dhakeswari Mandir. Since 1950 he has been living in Calcutta with his family and sometime in February, 1972 he alone entered into Bangladesh taking opportunity of relation given by the Bangladesh Government to the returnees for entry into Bangladesh from India. It has been further stated that he has been pushed out to West Bengal through Benapole border on 15.4.74 in pursuance of an order issued by Home Department on 12.4.74 and the order were duly executed. It was denied by the respondents that the order dated 12.4.74 were issued under the influence of Hem Chandra Chakravorty or anyone else. It was further stated that a specific case under Control of Entry Act was started against him for specific offence and this does not relate to the preventive detention, and that the order of detention was passed for the prejudicial activity of the detenue as contemplated under the Special Powers Act and the said prejudicial acts as shown in the grounds of detention relate to the period prior to his arrest on 12.6.74. The detenue started prejudicial activities after coming over to. Bangladesh in February, 1972. But as he is a national of a friendly country of Bangladesh, the Government thought it proper to push him out of Bangladesh instead of arresting him or starting a case against him. So he was physically pushed out to India on 15.4.74, but when he was again fund in Dacca without any valid travel document he was arrested on 12.6.74 and a case under the Control of Entry Act was started. It was further stated by the respondents that as there was reasonable apprehension and every chance that the detenue would again indulge himself in doing prejudicial activity on getting bail in the specific case, there was no other alternative but to pass an order of detention under the Special Powers Act and as such the order of detention was passed bona fide on the basis of materials which relate to his activities prior to his arrest on 12.6.74. It was further stated that there were materials before the detaining authority for its satisfaction that the detention of the detenue was necessary under the facts and circumstance of the case. It was further stated Hem Chandra Chakravorty is the present priest and care-taker of the temple. It was also stated that there were materials upon which the authority was satisfied and then passed the order of detention under the Emergency Power Rules after revoking the order under the Special Powers Act and the order of detention was valid in the eye of law. It was further submitted that the revocation of the earlier order does not debar the authority to pass the order of detention under the Emergency Powers Rules, 1975. 

 13. On an examination of the said grounds it appears that except Ground No.1 (b), none of the other grounds are relatable to the object of detention. It appears to us that the other grounds have relevance more with the dispute between the co-sharers, namely, the detenue and Hem Ch. Chakraboty over possession, management and disposal of the temple property, that with the object of detention under the Special Powers Act. The respondents have admitted that till 1950 before the detenue migrated to India, he was Shebait of the temple and according to them at present Hem Chandra Chakraboty is the care take and the priest of the temple property. It is the detenu's case that he is the owner of the temple property and the said Hem Chandra Chakraborty was given a share of the temple property by the detenu's father. It is apparent that there is a dispute between the detenue and Hem Chakraboty over the temple property and the said Hem Chandra lodged F.I.R. at Lalbagh P.S. over which a case under the Control of Entry Act was started against the detenue. It appears to us that the activities, alleged in the grounds of detention against the detenue can appropriately be dealt with otherwise under the ordinary law of the land.
